bugs.name: Entering 0, clearing, or entering an invalid row limit keeps the previous limit
bugs.summary: Typing 0 or an invalid value into the notebook Row limit, or clearing it, keeps running the previous limit, and reopening the editor shows the old value.
bugs.expected: Reject an invalid row limit with clear validation before running, rather than silently executing the previous limit.
bugs.actual: The field displayed 0 before running, but Visualize returned five rows and reopening Editor showed 5. A whole-page multimodal assertion confirmed no warning, validation error or notification explained the rejection/reset.
reproSteps: Create a fresh question from Sample Database > Products.
Sort Price ascending, set row limit 5, visualize, and save with a unique QA-RESULT name.
Reopen Editor, replace row limit 5 with 0 and blur the field.
Click Visualize, then reopen Editor.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: the row limit deliberately ignores values below 1, as Metabase's own tests assert.

bugs.name: Fractional row limit 2.5 is silently changed to 2 when running the query
bugs.summary: Fractional row limit 2.5 is silently changed to 2 when running the query.
bugs.expected: Require a positive whole-number limit with validation instead of silently changing an entered fractional value.
bugs.actual: Input displayed 2.5, but Visualize returned two rows and reopening Editor displayed 2. Whole-page multimodal assertion confirmed no message explaining the truncation.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Sample Database > Products question, sort Price ascending and set row limit 5.
Visualize and save with a unique QA-RESULT name; reopen Editor.
Replace row limit with 2.5 and blur.
Click Visualize, then reopen Editor.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: the row limit is converted to a whole number by design.

bugs.name: Undoing SQL deletion loses saved variable types and defaults
bugs.summary: Undoing SQL deletion loses saved variable types and defaults.
bugs.expected: Undo should restore the query's variable definitions and defaults together with the restored SQL text, preserving the query's ability to run.
bugs.actual: SELECT {{value}} AS selected_value is restored verbatim, but Number changes to Text and default42 disappears. Running fails: Cannot run the query: missing required parameters: #{"value"}. Also reproduced with a saved custom dropdown: it reverts to Input box and loses custom values/defaultalpha.
reproSteps: Choose New > SQL query > Sample Database and enter SELECT {{value}} AS selected_value.
Open Variables, set value's Variable type to Number and its default value to42. Run and confirm result42.
Save with a unique name. Reload the saved question from its clean question URL and confirm it still runs using default42.
Open Editor and Variables; verify Number and default42 are present.
Focus the SQL editor, press Ctrl+A, Backspace, then Ctrl+Z to undo the deletion.
Run the restored SQL. Observe missing-parameter error; Variables now shows Text with no default.
bugs.reason: Deleting a SQL variable discards its settings; undo restores only the query text, so the recreated variable starting with default settings is expected.

bugs.name: Saved-question onboarding dialog fails to close
bugs.summary: Saved-question onboarding dialog fails to close.
bugs.expected: Start exploring dismisses the onboarding dialog and lets the user interact with the saved question.
bugs.actual: After saving and reopening a question, clicking Start exploring twice left “It's okay to play around with saved questions” visible and blocking the editor. Escape also failed. Each dismissal attempted PUT /api/user/1/modal/qbnewb and received HTTP 500 with response “Internal server error.” A later full reload cleared the dialog.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai on a fresh fixture where the saved-question onboarding has not yet been acknowledged.
Open /question/notebook; select Sample Database > Orders.
Choose Count of rows under Summarize and Created At under grouping; click Visualize.
Save with a unique question name, then reload the saved question URL.
In “It's okay to play around with saved questions”, click Start exploring. Observe the dialog remains; repeat or press Escape to reproduce the failed dismissal.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review.

bugs.name: Notebook grouping and sort chips ignore advertised keyboard reorder controls
bugs.summary: Notebook grouping and sort chips ignore advertised keyboard reorder controls.
bugs.expected: With the second chip focused, Space should pick it up, ArrowLeft should move it before the first chip, and Space should drop it, as the accessible instructions specify.
bugs.actual: Space does not activate dragging or update live status. ArrowLeft then Space leaves the order unchanged. Independently reproduced with grouping in two browser sessions and with two sort chips, including normal Tab navigation. Wrappers have role=button, tabindex=0, aria-disabled=false and aria-roledescription=sortable. The screen-reader instructions say 'To pick up a draggable item, press the space bar. While dragging, use the arrow keys to move the item...'.
reproSteps: Open /question/notebook and choose Sample Database > Products.
Choose Count of rows as the summary, Category as the first grouping column, then add Vendor as the second grouping column.
Use Tab navigation until the Vendor grouping chip has keyboard focus.
Press Space, ArrowLeft, then Space.
Observe that the chip is never picked up and the grouping order remains Category, Vendor.
The same failure occurs after adding Sort Category followed by Vendor and focusing the Vendor sort wrapper (Tab past the first chip's Change direction button).
bugs.reason: Not a product bug for labeling: the missing keyboard reorder is an accessibility-only issue with no visible or pointer-driven defect.

bugs.name: Deleting a source question makes its owned dependent View-only, preventing source repair
bugs.summary: Deleting a source question makes its owned dependent View-only, preventing source repair.
bugs.expected: Missing source should produce an error but the question owner should retain Editor access to replace the deleted source and repair the dependent.
bugs.actual: Dependent changes to View-only, displays 'Card 74 does not exist.', and removes Editor and other query-edit controls. Default multimodal assertion confirmed no Editor or source-change control exists anywhere on the page; owner cannot repair the saved query.
reproSteps: Disposable source#74 QA-SOURCE-People-Delete-1021 is permanently deleted; dependent#75 QA-SOURCE-People-Child-1021 remains for inspection. Create fresh owned fixtures for independent reproduction.
Create an owned saved raw People question using Sample Database.
Create and save an owned dependent using that question as source, Count grouped by Source.
Move the source to trash, reload it, and Delete permanently with confirmation.
Open the dependent and expand error details.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: permanently deleting a source question is documented to break questions built on it; the dependent stays editable through its notebook URL.

bugs.name: Saving query edits from a stale tab silently undoes a separately saved question rename
bugs.summary: Saving query edits from a stale tab silently undoes a separately saved question rename.
bugs.expected: Saving only the row-limit edit should retain the independently saved title, or warn that it will overwrite a newer saved rename.
bugs.actual: Six rows are saved, but the title returns to SAVE Orders five save-as 1021, undoing the first tab's saved rename. A whole-page AI assertion confirmed the old title, six rows, and no conflict warning after save. Replace dialog had displayed the stale name; no title was edited in that tab.
reproSteps: Create a Sample Database Orders question, add Row limit 5, Visualize and save with a unique SAVE-prefixed name.
Open the same saved question in a second browser tab using the same session.
In the second tab use Editor to change Row limit to 6, then Visualize without saving.
In the first tab rename the question inline to SAVE Orders renamed while editing 1021 and press Enter; the new title is shown.
Return to the second tab, click Save and keep Replace original question selected, then Save.
Reload the question and inspect title and row count.
bugs.reason: Works as intended per human review.

bugs.name: Dragging custom columns to reorder the notebook leaves results in their old column order
bugs.summary: Dragging custom columns to reorder the notebook leaves results in their old column order.
bugs.expected: Reordering custom columns should make the generated results use the corresponding new order, or clearly indicate that result ordering is separate.
bugs.actual: Notebook changed from Net Delta, Triple, Band, Upper Band to Upper Band, Triple, Band, Net Delta. After Visualize the results still showed Net Delta, Triple, Band, Upper Band. Values remained correct.
reproSteps: Use fresh test-owned question. No chart settings were intentionally changed. Result values are correct; suspicion concerns only mismatch between notebook's reordered expression chips and result order, which may have a separate intended ordering model.
Using primary fixture identity, create a fresh Orders query in Sample Database.
Add [Total] - [Subtotal] named QACOL Net Delta; [QACOL Net Delta] * 3 named QACOL Triple; case([Quantity] > 3, "Bulk", "Single") named QACOL Band; upper([QACOL Band]) named QACOL Upper Band.
Visualize and save under a unique QACOL-prefixed name. Reload and open Editor.
Drag QACOL Upper Band chip onto QACOL Net Delta chip; observe notebook order Upper Band, Triple, Band, Net Delta.
Click Visualize and inspect custom column ordering in results.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: table column order is a visualization setting, separate from the order of custom-expression chips in the notebook; values are unaffected.

bugs.name: A restored question is absent from its Saved in collection
bugs.summary: A restored question is absent from its designated Saved in collection.
bugs.expected: The restored question appears in the collection its Info panel lists.
bugs.actual: Following the Saved in link to Harbor Admin's Personal Collection reveals the question is missing from the list, which ends alphabetically at QA-SUMMARY.
reproSteps: Create and save a unique QA-UNDO Sample Database Orders question in Harbor Admin's Personal Collection.
Trash it, then click toast Undo while visible.
Refresh question: it remains restored and Orders query/results are intact.
Open More info and follow the Saved in Harbor Admin's Personal Collection link. Inspect the complete table and refresh it.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce: restored questions stay listed in their collection; the original run likely overlapped other agents' changes in the shared sandbox.

bugs.name: New custom-column editor returns to saved results while entering the column name, discarding the draft
bugs.summary: New custom-column editor returns to saved results while entering the column name, discarding the draft.
bugs.expected: Entering a custom-column name should leave the editor open with the formula and name available to commit using Done.
bugs.actual: After typing QACOL Discount Zero the page showed saved results rather than the custom-column editor. Reopening Editor showed only the previously saved columns; an assertion confirmed QACOL Discount Zero was not present.
reproSteps: Create a fresh QACOL-prefixed copy of an Orders question with custom columns and save it.
Save an additional custom column, reload the saved question, then open Editor.
Click the plus beside the custom columns and enter coalesce([Discount], 0).
Enter QACOL Discount Zero in the column-name field without clicking Done.
Observe the page return to saved results; reopen Editor to inspect the draft.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review.

bugs.name: Reload silently drops rejected Number parameter and runs query without the filter
bugs.summary: Reload silently drops rejected Number parameter and runs query without the filter.
bugs.expected: Preserve the rejected filter value with validation feedback or display an explanation, rather than silently running the query with the filter omitted.
bugs.actual: Refreshing the page clears the invalid 'oops' value from the Minimum parameter input back to its placeholder and displays count 3 from executing the query without the condition, with no error or explanation.
reproSteps: Save a SQL question on Products that filters p.PRICE between 10.5 and 20.75 and has an optional Number parameter minimum ([[AND p.ID > {{minimum}}]]).
Enter oops in Minimum and run. The query reports For input string: "oops" and URL contains minimum=oops.
Refresh the browser page.
bugs.reason: Works as intended per human review.

bugs.name: Trash toast Undo leaves the question in trash with editing disabled
bugs.summary: Trash toast Undo leaves the question in trash with editing disabled.
bugs.expected: Clicking Undo in the toast restores the question from trash. The banner goes away, and Filter, Summarize and Editor become available again.
bugs.actual: The toast closes, but the question stays in trash. The banner remains and editing controls stay hidden. The only update request sent is the original move to trash; no restore request is sent. After a refresh, the breadcrumb shows Trash and the banner offers Restore, Move and Delete permanently.
reproSteps: As an admin, save an Orders question in your personal collection and open it.
Click the ellipsis (…) in the question header, choose Move to trash, then click Move to trash in the dialog.
While the "has been moved to the trash" toast is visible at the bottom left, click its Undo button.
Look at the page: the red trash banner is still there and Filter, Summarize and Editor are missing. Refresh the page: the question is still in Trash.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review.

bugs.name: Relative date filter silently changes an entered 0-day interval to 1 day
bugs.summary: Relative date filter silently changes an entered 0-day interval to 1 day.
bugs.expected: Reject an unsupported zero interval with clear validation, or retain the entered interval rather than silently changing it.
bugs.actual: Entering 0 in the relative date filter interval field is accepted with an enabled 'Update filter' button and no validation error. Applying the filter turns it into 'Created At is yesterday', and reopening the filter shows the interval field changed to 1 day.
reproSteps: Create a Sample Database Orders question and choose Created At → Relative date range → Previous.
Enter 0 in Interval with days selected and Include today off.
Click Add/Update filter; reopen the filter.
Save as a separate QA-DATE question, reload and open Editor and the date filter.
bugs.reason: Works as intended per human review.

bugs.name: Numeric multi-value Equal to filter returns No results despite selecting a price present in Products
bugs.summary: Numeric multi-value Equal to filter returns No results despite selecting a price present in Products.
bugs.expected: Equal to selections 20.5 or 25.1 should include the previously displayed product with Price 25.1.
bugs.actual: The query displays No results! and Showing 0 rows, although the filter editor contains 25.1 and the preceding range results included that exact price.
reproSteps: Choose Sample Database > Products in the notebook.
Add Price Between 20.5 and 30.5, then Visualize. Results show 24 rows, including Products ID 15 with Price 25.1.
Open the Price filter and change Between to Equal to.
Enter 25.1 in the number input, press Enter and click Update filter.
Reopen the resulting Price is equal to 2 selections chip; it contains 20.5 and 25.1 while results show No results.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: the products are priced 25.09876…, displayed rounded to 25.1; exact-equality filters on the rounded value correctly match nothing.

bugs.name: Nonnumeric range minimum abc is silently discarded, changing Between into Less than or equal
bugs.summary: Nonnumeric range minimum abc is silently discarded, changing Between into Less than or equal.
bugs.expected: Nonnumeric minimum should be rejected with validation, not silently treated as an empty minimum and converted into a different filter.
bugs.actual: abc is discarded and Between becomes ID is less than or equal to 3.
reproSteps: Create Products question in Sample Database and filter ID Between 1 and 3.
Visualize; open ID filter.
Replace Min 1 with abc, leaving Max 3, then click Update filter.
Observe filter changes to ID is less than or equal to 3 and returns three rows.
bugs.reason: Works as intended per human review.

bugs.name: Joining People to a saved state-count question fails with a session-timeout error
bugs.summary: Joining People to a saved state-count question fails with a session-timeout error.
bugs.expected: The supported saved-question join returns People rows with their corresponding state count, or null for unmatched states.
bugs.actual: The query ends with 'There was a problem with your question'. Error details begin 'Statement was canceled or the session timed out; SQL statement:'. No joined results are returned.
reproSteps: Create a fresh builder question from Sample Database Orders.
Join Products on Orders.Product ID = Products.ID (inner join), then People on Orders.User ID = People.ID (left join).
Filter Products.Category to Gizmo, summarize Count grouped by People.State, run and save with a unique QA-JOIN-State-Gizmo name. The source returns 48 state groups.
Create another new builder question using Sample Database People.
Add a left join, search for and select the newly saved state-count question.
Set People.State = the saved question's People - User → State; leave all joined fields selected.
Click Visualize and wait for completion, then open Show error details.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: the join is built correctly, and the timeout comes from the H2 sample database re-evaluating the joined subquery for every row. That is a sample-data performance limit, not a product bug.

bugs.name: Previously working notebook deep link opens blank after replacing its builder question with SQL
bugs.summary: Previously working notebook deep link opens blank after replacing its builder question with SQL.
bugs.expected: The existing notebook deep link should redirect to or display the question's native SQL editor/results, or offer a usable way to open them.
bugs.actual: Same question title loads with completely blank body. The normal saved-question URL still displays results.
reproSteps: Create a Sample Database Orders notebook joined to Products on Product ID = ID, save with a QA-CONVERT prefix.
Open Editor on the saved question and retain its generated /question/<id>-<slug>/notebook URL.
View SQL, Convert this question to SQL, Save, and choose Replace original question.
Refresh normal saved question URL and verify SQL results load.
Open the original notebook URL that worked before conversion.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: after a question becomes SQL it has no notebook view, so its old notebook URL no longer applies; the page still offers a way back to the results.

bugs.name: Reopening a saved Time grouping parameter prevents inspecting or changing its field mapping
bugs.summary: Reopening a saved Time grouping parameter prevents inspecting or changing its field mapping.
bugs.expected: The saved parameter should display its mapped field and clicking its mapping selector should offer table/field choices.
bugs.actual: After reopening the saved question, the mapping selector displays Select… and clicking its text or arrow shows no usable menu. The existing query still returns yearly results.
reproSteps: Create a Sample Database native SQL question: SELECT {{grouping}} AS period, COUNT(*) AS n FROM PEOPLE GROUP BY period ORDER BY period.
Set grouping type Time grouping, map to People > Created At and set default Year. Run and save as a fresh question.
Refresh or reopen saved question, click Open Editor and Variables.
Field to map to shows Select… instead of People / Created At. Click that selector, including its arrow.
No table or field choices appear, preventing remapping.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review.

bugs.name: Question-backed SQL parameter list falls back to text input and does not recover after source column is restored
bugs.summary: Question-backed SQL parameter list falls back to text input and does not recover after source column is restored.
bugs.expected: After restoring the original source column, the saved question-backed list should offer the four source categories again, or provide actionable dependency feedback.
bugs.actual: After source restoration and a full consumer refresh, Category still opens an empty free-text input with disabled Add filter, not the four values. Opening selectable-value settings after the column change showed an empty source picker. No consumer changes were saved.
reproSteps: Create own saved SQL source: SELECT DISTINCT CATEGORY FROM PRODUCTS ORDER BY CATEGORY.
Create a SQL consumer: SELECT ID, CATEGORY FROM PRODUCTS WHERE CATEGORY = {{category}} ORDER BY ID LIMIT 10. Configure Text category dropdown values from source question CATEGORY; save.
Reload consumer; observe four categories and execute Gizmo successfully.
Edit source to SELECT DISTINCT CATEGORY AS CHANGED_CATEGORY FROM PRODUCTS ORDER BY CATEGORY; run and replace saved source.
Open consumer parameter: it now shows a free-text input instead of selectable values.
Restore the source SQL to the original CATEGORY column; run and save. Reload the consumer and reopen Category.
bugs.reason: Works as intended per human review.

bugs.name: Native SQL date parameter silently converts invalid February 29, 2023 to March 1, 2023
bugs.summary: Native SQL date parameter silently converts invalid February 29, 2023 to March 1, 2023.
bugs.expected: An impossible calendar date should be rejected with validation rather than silently used as a different day.
bugs.actual: On leaving the input, 02/29/2023 changes to March 1, 2023. Updating and running uses March 1, 2023 in both filter chip and result.
reproSteps: Using the primary fixture account, select New > SQL query and Sample Database.
Enter SELECT CAST({{day}} AS DATE) AS chosen_day; and set day variable type to Date.
Open Day filter, enter 02/29/2024, add filter and run; observe February 29, 2024.
Reopen Day filter, replace date with 02/29/2023 and leave the date input.
Click Update filter and run the query.
bugs.reason: Works as intended per human review.

bugs.name: Decimal post-summary Between filter excludes quarter whose displayed total equals upper bound
bugs.summary: Decimal post-summary Between filter excludes quarter whose displayed total equals upper bound.
bugs.expected: Filtering between displayed totals 123889.6 and 132631.24 should retain both Q2 and Q3 2027.
bugs.actual: Only Q2 2027 remains in the result table; Q3 2027 (previously displaying 132,631.24) is excluded when using that value as the upper bound.
reproSteps: Use Orders, filter Created At Jan 1–Dec 31 2027.
Summarize Count, Average of Total, Sum of Total, Minimum of Total and Maximum of Total by Created At Quarter and Quantity with Don't bin.
Add second summary Count, Sum of Count and Sum of Sum of Total, grouped by inherited Created At Quarter; run. Q2 displays 123889.6 and Q3 displays 132631.24.
Add a subsequent Filter on Sum of Sum of Total Between 123889.6 and 132631.24; run and inspect results.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: the filter compares the stored total (132631.2439…), which is above the bound; only the display rounds to 132,631.24.

bugs.name: Renaming a custom summary aggregate to match an existing column name silently breaks post-aggregation filtering and returns no results
bugs.summary: Renaming a custom summary aggregate to match an existing column name silently breaks post-aggregation filtering and returns no results.
bugs.expected: Renaming the custom aggregation should maintain correct filter field bindings or prevent naming collisions with existing columns.
bugs.actual: Renaming the aggregation to 'Category' produces duplicate column names and causes the query to return 'No results!' (0 rows).
reproSteps: As Harbor Admin, create a fresh QA-SUMMARY question from Sample Database Products.
Add custom Count() named Price and Count()*10 named Category, grouped by source Category. Sort second aggregate descending.
Add post-summary numeric aggregate Category between 500 and 535; results are Gadget 53/530 and Gizmo 51/510. Save and reopen.
Add post-summary text grouping Category is Gadget; verify Gadget 53/530.
Edit the first custom aggregate name from Price to Category, leaving Count() unchanged. Click Update, then Visualize.
bugs.reason: Works as intended per human review.

bugs.name: Date parameter Update filter silently discards invalid typed date and closes calendar with previous date applied
bugs.summary: Date parameter Update filter silently discards invalid typed date and closes calendar with previous date applied.
bugs.expected: Invalid typed date should be rejected with validation feedback and keep the editor open for correction rather than silently dismissing.
bugs.actual: Update filter remains enabled, closes the calendar on click, and retains May 15, 2025 with no validation error or feedback displayed.
reproSteps: As default account, choose New > SQL query > Sample Database.
Create a fresh QA-PARAM question with SQL SELECT ID, CREATED_AT, TOTAL FROM ORDERS WHERE CREATED_AT >= {{start_date}} ORDER BY CREATED_AT LIMIT 10.
Configure start_date as Date and default May 15, 2025. Run, save the fresh question, and reopen.
Open Start Date calendar and replace Date text with not-a-date.
Click Update filter.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: unparseable typed text is ignored and the last valid date, still shown in the calendar, stays applied.

bugs.name: Renaming a saved source custom column breaks a previously working downstream custom expression
bugs.summary: Renaming a saved source custom column breaks a previously working downstream custom expression.
bugs.expected: Renaming the source custom column should preserve the downstream expression dependency, or the rename workflow should handle dependent saved questions instead of leaving a previously valid question broken.
bugs.actual: The downstream question displays “There was a problem with your question”; details say Column "source.QA-EXPR-DiscountZero" not found. The source question itself still runs after the rename.
reproSteps: Create a QA-EXPR source question from Sample Database Orders with custom column QA-EXPR-DiscountZero = coalesce([Discount], 0), then save it.

Create a second QA-EXPR question using the saved source question. Add QA-EXPR-SafeDivide = case([QA-EXPR-DiscountZero] = 0, 0, 10 / [QA-EXPR-DiscountZero]). Visualize, save and refresh; valid numeric results appear.
Reopen the source question editor, rename QA-EXPR-DiscountZero to QA-EXPR-ZeroRenamed, Update, Visualize, then Save over the source question.
Reopen the downstream saved question and expand Show error details.
bugs.reason: Works as intended per human review.

bugs.name: Selecting second custom label for duplicate parameter value displays the first label instead
bugs.summary: Selecting second custom label for duplicate parameter value displays the first label instead.
bugs.expected: The selected Second label should remain displayed, or duplicate underlying values with conflicting labels should be rejected during configuration.
bugs.actual: Both First label and Second label are offered in the dropdown, but selecting Second label causes First label to be selected and displayed in the filter parameter. Running the query returns 9 Gizmo rows while displaying First label.
reproSteps: Create an own native Sample Database question: SELECT ID, TITLE, CATEGORY, PRICE FROM PRODUCTS WHERE CATEGORY = {{category}} AND PRICE >= {{min_price}} ORDER BY ID.

Configure category as Text, Dropdown list, single value. Enter custom list lines Gizmo,First label; Gizmo,Second label; Widget,Widget label, with each on its own line. Configure min_price Number with default80.5.
Open category widget, choose Second label and click Update filter.
Run the query and inspect the parameter label.
bugs.reason: Works as intended per human review.

bugs.name: SQL database switch leaves Data Reference showing the previous database's PRODUCTS schema
bugs.summary: SQL database switch leaves Data Reference showing the previous database's PRODUCTS schema.
bugs.expected: After changing SQL database, Data Reference should reset or show tables belonging to the chosen database rather than suggest an unavailable table.
bugs.actual: After switching from Sample Database to Release operations, sidebar still displays PRODUCTS with ID, EAN, TITLE, CATEGORY, VENDOR, PRICE, RATING, CREATED_AT and Orders/Reviews connections. Running the preserved products query now returns ERROR: relation "products" does not exist.
reproSteps: Using the primary fixture session, create a fresh question via New > SQL query > Sample Database; no existing QA question is required.
Enter SELECT p.id, p.title, o.id AS order_id FROM products p JOIN orders o ON o.product_id = p.id WHERE p.id = 1 ORDER BY o.id LIMIT 2; and run.
In Data Reference open PRODUCTS.
Change the database dropdown above the SQL editor to Release operations.
Run the preserved query and observe the PRODUCTS sidebar beside the relation-does-not-exist error.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: Data Reference is a browser that spans databases, and it accurately shows the Sample Database table the user opened. Nothing requires it to reset when the SQL editor's database changes. The query error is correct for the newly selected database, which has no products table.

bugs.name: Snippet editor allows saving whitespace-only SQL code
bugs.summary: Snippet editor allows saving whitespace-only SQL code.
bugs.expected: Whitespace-only code should be rejected rather than saving a blank reusable snippet.
bugs.actual: Save accepted three spaces and closed the dialog without error. After refresh and reopening, the snippet SQL field remains blank whitespace.
reproSteps: Start a fresh SQL question on Sample Database and open SQL Snippets.
Create an own QA-REF snippet with SQL SELECT TITLE FROM PRODUCTS WHERE CATEGORY = 'Gizmo' and a unique QA-REF name.
Expand its sidebar entry and Edit. Clear all code: Save is disabled.
Enter exactly three spaces as the code and Save.
Refresh, reopen SQL Snippets and Edit the same snippet.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: snippets may contain partial SQL, and Metabase's docs let authors save broken code at their own risk. The value is saved exactly as typed and shown accurately, and inserting it causes no error or data loss. This is a loose validation rule, not a breakage.

bugs.name: Changing a custom column's type bypasses validation of dependent expressions and filters
bugs.summary: Changing a custom column's type keeps dependent expressions and filters that no longer fit it, such as a text Contains filter on a column changed to a number, and the query fails when run.
bugs.expected: Editing the upstream expression should revalidate dependent expressions and identify the incompatible dependency before allowing the question to remain apparently valid, consistent with validation when entering the same dependent expression.
bugs.actual: Changing Upstream amount from [Total] * 2 to the string literal "text" is accepted while Downstream amount = [Upstream amount] / 2 is retained. Preview fails with 'Data conversion error converting "text"'. Opening the downstream editor initially enables Update; retyping the identical formula shows 'Types are incompatible.' and disables Update. The broken query can be saved and fails again after reload.
reproSteps: Sign in and choose New → Question → Sample Database → Orders.
Add a Custom column with expression [Total] * 2 and name Upstream amount. Click Done.
Add another custom column with expression [Upstream amount] / 2 and name Downstream amount. Click Done. Preview to confirm numeric results.
Edit Upstream amount and replace its formula with the string literal "text" (including quotes). Click Update.
Click the Custom column step's play/Preview button. Observe a data conversion error instead of results.
Open Downstream amount. Observe that Update is initially enabled. Replace the formula with the identical [Upstream amount] / 2, and observe 'Types are incompatible.' with Update disabled.
Cancel editing and optionally save the question. Reload and run it to confirm that the invalid dependent expression persists and the query still fails.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: the user made an incompatible change to the upstream column and the query then fails with a clear error. It can be fixed by editing the downstream formula or editing or removing the incompatible filter, unlike a column that silently disappears (querying-496).

bugs.name: SQL variable settings save an empty default even when Default filter widget value is marked required
bugs.summary: SQL variable settings save an empty default even when Default filter widget value is marked required.
bugs.expected: With Always require a value enabled and the default field marked required, saving should require a default or clearly explain that an empty default is allowed.
bugs.actual: Clearing fallback leaves the default field marked (required), but Save successfully replaces the question.
reproSteps: Using the primary fixture, create a new SQL query on Sample Database: SELECT {{value}} AS PARAM_VALUE.
Set text variable default to fallback, save a fresh QA-PARAM question.
Enable Always require a value and save replacing the original.
Clear fallback using the x in Default filter widget value. The field shows (required).
Save and confirm replacement.
Refresh and open the editor's Variables settings.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: Metabase treats a required SQL variable as an execution constraint, and its tests cover a required variable with no default. Running the question asks for a value, and entering one runs it normally.

bugs.name: Discarding an unsaved SQL edit via Back to previous results leaves the discarded query and zero-row results visible
bugs.summary: Discarding an unsaved SQL edit via Back to previous results leaves the discarded query and zero-row results visible.
bugs.expected: Discarding restores the saved question and its two-row results, rather than continuing to show discarded SQL.
bugs.actual: Dialog closes and URL becomes the saved question's URL, but header still says New question, editor still contains ID = 999999 and No results/Showing 0 rows remain.
reproSteps: Create a fresh SQL question on Sample Database using SELECT ID, TITLE, CATEGORY, PRICE FROM PRODUCTS WHERE ID <= 2 ORDER BY ID; run and save with a unique QALIFE name.
Reopen it and Open Editor; replace SQL with SELECT ID, TITLE FROM PRODUCTS WHERE ID = 999999 and run.
On No results, click Back to previous results.
In Discard your changes dialog, click Cancel; verify unsaved SQL remains.

bugs.name: Excluding days of the week drops the wrong days (and ignores some selected days)
bugs.summary: Excluding days of the week drops the wrong days (and ignores some selected days).
bugs.expected: Orders by Created At: Day of week gives 1=2678, 2=2719, 3=2590, 4=2776, 5=2646, 6=2690, 7=2661 (total 18760). Excluding day 1 should return 16082. Excluding days 1 and 7 should return 13421. Excluding days 3 and 5 should return 13524. Each matches native SQL `day_of_week(created_at) not in (...)`.
bugs.actual: != 1 returns 16041 (removes day 2 / Monday). != 1,7 also returns 16041: the SQL is only `extract(iso_day_of_week ...) <> 1 OR CREATED_AT IS NULL`, so the 7 is dropped entirely. != 3,5 returns 13323, with SQL `iso_day_of_week <> 3 AND iso_day_of_week <> 6`. By contrast, the SQL for = 1 is `(extract(iso_day_of_week ...) % 7) + 1 = 1`, which correctly returns 2678.
reproSteps: Sign in, then New > Question > Sample Database > Orders. Summarize Count by Created At: Day of week and note the per-day counts.

Send the same query through the API (POST /api/dataset) with a legacy numeric MBQL filter excluding Sunday and Saturday: ['!=', ['field', <Created At field id>, {'temporal-unit': 'day-of-week'}], 1, 7].
Observe the count is 16041 rather than 13421, and the native SQL (POST /api/dataset/native) contains only iso_day_of_week <> 1.
Send the filter with only 1: it also returns 16041 rather than 16082, while the = 1 filter returns the correct 2678.
For comparison, the UI Filter > Created At > Exclude > Days of the week picker excludes the right days.
bugs.reason: Out of scope: only reachable through the API with legacy numeric MBQL; the UI Exclude picker and 'Not on' drill exclude the right days.

bugs.name: Join type menu ignores Escape and arrow-key navigation
bugs.summary: The query builder's join type menu opens from the keyboard but does not respond to Escape or Arrow Down. Focus remains on 'Change join type'; the menu remains open. Reproduced using mouse and keyboard opening on multiple Orders→Products queries. Evidence: dogfood-output/screenshots/issue-003-step-1.png, issue-003-step-2.png, and issue-003-focus.json.
bugs.expected: Escape closes the join type menu and arrow keys navigate its menu items after opening it with the keyboard.
bugs.actual: Escape does not dismiss the menu, arrow keys do not navigate its options, and focus remains on the trigger while the popup stays open.
reproSteps: Create a Sample Database Orders question and join Products, or open saved question /question/42-qa-joined-custom-summary/notebook.
Focus the Change join type button and press Enter; Left outer join, Right outer join, and Inner join appear.
Press Escape; the menu stays open.
Press Arrow Down; focus stays on Change join type instead of moving into the menu options. Pressing Tab moves to the Products button behind the menu.
bugs.reason: Excluded by the browser bug-reproducer pure-accessibility rule. This report establishes only keyboard/focus/accessibility semantics or a generic contrast threshold, without an explicit supplied product requirement or documented promise for that behavior. Ordinary pointer functionality or visible setting values are not alleged to fail. This negative reference is scoped to the reported accessibility-only claim; it does not cover independently demonstrated data loss, pointer failures, or an explicitly documented keyboard action.
